industries.retail.title: Cleaning robots for malls and stores | Professional Robotics
industries.retail.description: Cleaning robots for malls and supermarkets: concourses, sales floor, parking, promo robots. Lenta and Perekrestok case studies, a 26-mall Moscow pilot.
industries.retail.name: Shopping centers and retail
industries.retail.lead: A cleaning robot for shopping centers washes concourses, the sales floor and parking on a schedule: at night before opening and by day between shoppers.
industries.retail.lead2: Cleaners stay where hands are needed: restrooms, the food court, spills at the checkout. The robot takes the repeat passes over large areas.
industries.retail.primaryCta.label: Discuss a mall pilot
industries.retail.secondaryCta.label: Calculate payback
industries.retail.hero.proof.title: Moscow pilot · 26 malls
industries.retail.hero.proof.status: Pilot under way. Robots from Russian manufacturers clean sales floors and parking, and will then be compared with manual cleaning. Results aren’t published yet.
industries.retail.photo.alt: A floor-scrubbing robot washes the central concourse of a shopping center in the early morning, with store shutters still down
industries.retail.heads.directions: What we automate in a mall or store.
industries.retail.problems.lead: Fewer people are available for cleaning, for reasons a store can’t influence.
industries.retail.problems.items.0.title: Cleaning depends on migrant labor.
industries.retail.problems.items.0.text: Over 80% of cleaning staff are foreign nationals. In 2025, 11 regions introduced additional restrictions on hiring them.
industries.retail.problems.items.1.title: Payroll is rising.
industries.retail.problems.items.1.text: In five years, cleaning companies’ payroll has grown two- to threefold. That goes into the cleaning contract price.
industries.retail.problems.items.2.title: Frontline staff are scarce.
industries.retail.problems.items.2.text: 15% of retailers name frontline staff shortages as their main reason to modernize.
industries.retail.problems.items.3.title: Large area, short window.
industries.retail.problems.items.3.text: Concourses, sales floor and parking must be washed before opening, then cleaned by day without disturbing shoppers.
industries.retail.frequency.title: The sales floor is cleaned several times a day.
industries.retail.frequency.lead: Each cleaning is a separate pass over the entire area. The more passes, the more sense it makes to give them to a robot and leave spot work to people.
industries.retail.frequency.mainTitle: How many times a day a store is cleaned.
industries.retail.frequency.items.0.aria: Sales floor, regular day: 2 times a day
industries.retail.frequency.items.1.aria: Sales floor, fall and winter: 5 times a day
industries.retail.frequency.items.2.aria: Produce, all day: 5 to 10 times a day
industries.retail.frequency.note: As Perekrestok (X5 Group) puts it: this is the chain’s practice, not a sanitary standard.
industries.retail.frequency.service: 10–15 min a day to look after the robot; the docking station does the rest.
industries.retail.directions.items.0.tex: Floor-scrubbing robots wash mall concourses and the sales floor at night before opening, then make repeat passes by day among shoppers.
industries.retail.directions.items.1.tex: Sweeping and scrubbing robots for indoor and underground parking. In the Moscow pilot, robots clean not only the mall interiors but the parking too.
industries.retail.directions.items.2.tex: A service robot with an advertising screen carries promos around the floor and shows the way. BellaBot works this way in two Perekrestok stores; according to project participants, sales of some products grow by up to 100%.
industries.retail.directions.items.3.tex: Online order picking and moving goods behind the sales floor is warehouse robotics. It has a page of its own.
industries.retail.case.title: Chains already use floor robots.
industries.retail.case.lead: Named sites and figures come from open sources. These are not our projects but the market track record you can build on.
industries.retail.cases.items.0.title: Lenta hypermarkets: robots across the country.
industries.retail.cases.items.0.text: Volgograd, Nizhny Novgorod, Moscow, St Petersburg and other cities. They started with a pilot: 10 robots in 9 hypermarkets, then bought 32 more. Savings come from staff and from dropping rented scrubbers.
industries.retail.cases.items.0.quote: According to Lenta’s press service, cleaning staff shrank by 30–40%.
industries.retail.cases.items.1.title: Perekrestok: Pudu CC1 in the chain’s supermarkets.
industries.retail.cases.items.1.text: 9 stores in Moscow, 1 in St Petersburg, 1 in Sochi (as of June 2024). Caring for the robot with its docking station takes 10–15 minutes a day.
industries.retail.cases.items.1.quote: 11 tonnes of water a year per store versus 73 tonnes for a manual floor scrubber, according to project participants.
industries.retail.cases.items.2.title: Central Children’s Store: pilot week one.
industries.retail.cases.items.2.text: A pilot by FTs BAS under the Moscow Department of Entrepreneurship and Innovation: 26 malls, robots from four Russian manufacturers. They clean interiors and parking lots.
industries.retail.cases.items.2.quote: The pilot lasts several months, then a comparison with manual cleaning. No results published yet.
industries.retail.economy.title: Calculate the payback for a mall.
industries.retail.economy.lead: The model covers floor cleaning: area, schedule, robots needed and when they pay back. The “Mall” type is already selected.
industries.retail.economy.estimate: Indicative estimate This is a calculation from our model, not a deployment result. Figures for your site come after an assessment or pilot.
industries.retail.economy.note: Indicative estimate from our ROI (return on investment) model. A detailed estimate follows the site assessment.
industries.retail.vendorsLead: We match equipment to the area, flooring and cleaning schedule, without tying you to a single brand. The Moscow mall pilot runs on Russian robots.
industries.retail.why.title: Don’t wait for the city pilot.
industries.retail.why.text: The Moscow pilot promises its results after several months of operation. You don’t have to wait: we’ll launch a robot in one concourse or on one floor of your mall and compare it with manual cleaning using your own figures.
industries.retail.form.title: A robot for your mall or chain: let’s talk.
industries.retail.form.lead: We’ll review layout, zones and cleaning schedule, then propose equipment, an operating mode and a format: purchase, rental or cleaning as a service.
